title: Always Be My Maybe
about: A celebrity chef reconnects with her childhood best friend when she comes home to San Francisco.
cue: Serve the mains when Judy shows young Sasha how to make kimchi stew.

Mix it all up before eating.Hello Peril band wingsTwice-fried wings tossed in a sticky gochujang and honey glazeHow to make it1kg chicken wings1 L vegetable oil, for frying3 tbsp gochujang3 tbsp honey3 cloves of garlic1 tbsp sesame seedsFry the wings in the vegetable oil at 160°C, then rest.Fry again at 190°C until crackly.Warm the gochujang with honey and crushed garlic until glossy.Toss the wings through and scatter with sesame seeds.Tiny tasting menu salmon cucumber cupsThe absurd fancy dinner with the tiny plates and KeanuHow to make itAs written, serves 4Thick cucumber rounds hollowed into cups, filled with yuzu crème fraîche and cured salmon, finished with salmon roe and a single chive.Cut 2 continental cucumbers into 2cm thick rounds and scoop a hollow from each with a melon baller, leaving a base.Mix 100g crème fraîche with 1 tsp yuzu or lemon juice and a pinch of salt.Dice 150g smoked salmon finely.Spoon or pipe the cream into each cup, top with salmon, a few beads of salmon roe (40g total) and a short piece of chive.Serve on a long plate, deliberately small.Fried rice with a runny eggSasha's after-school dinner alone, before Judy taught her.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsKimchi jjigaeSpicy stew of pork belly and kimchi with gochugaru, simmered until richHow to make it400g pork belly, sliced2 tbsp vegetable oil300g kimchi, chopped2 cloves of garlic1 tbsp gochugaru750ml water300g firm tofu2 spring onionsSlice the pork and chop the kimchi.Fry the pork in the vegetable oil until browned, then add the kimchi, garlic and gochugaru.Pour in the water and simmer.Add sliced tofu and spring onion and simmer for the last few minutes.
